card.occupation: Principal structural engineer at a mid-sized engineering consultancy in Brighton, specialising in the assessment and repair of historic bridges and masonry structures. He works full-time, about 40 hours a week, split between the office, home and site visits.
card.education_detail: A-levels in Maths, Physics and Geography at a comprehensive school in Maidstone. BEng in Civil Engineering from the University of Bristol, graduating in 1984. He later became a Chartered Engineer and a Member of the Institution of Structural Engineers. Since then he has done various evening courses: Italian, life drawing and an Open University module on the history of science.
card.household: Lives with his wife Helen, 60, a part-time peripatetic music teacher, in a Victorian terraced house on a hill near the centre of Lewes. They have been married for 34 years. Their two grown-up children have left home: a daughter in Bristol and a son in Leeds. There are no pets at the moment; the old cat died last year and they haven't decided whether to get another.
card.cultural_background: White British, born in Maidstone, Kent, to a father who was a quantity surveyor and a mother who worked as a school secretary. He was brought up Church of England and still thinks of himself as Christian. He goes to the parish church perhaps once or twice a month and at Christmas and Easter, and his faith is quiet and more about practice than doctrine. He is comfortably middle class without making much of it, and reads the Guardian and the FT weekend edition about equally.
card.professional_persona: A thorough, unshowy engineer who is respected for being straight with clients about what a structure actually needs rather than what would be most lucrative. He enjoys the detective side of the job: old drawings, odd repairs from the 1920s, working out why a Victorian arch hasn't fallen down. He mentors graduates patiently and tends to give credit away. He is not especially tidy with paperwork and sometimes leaves reports later than he should, but he never cuts corners on the calculations.
card.sports_persona: Not a sports fan in the shouting sense. He walks a great deal on the South Downs, usually on Saturday mornings, and cycles to the station when the weather allows. He swam at school and still does an occasional early swim at the Pells Pool in summer. He'll watch the cricket on in the background, and Wimbledon with Helen, but he couldn't name the current England football squad.
card.arts_persona: Broad and curious tastes. He goes to Glyndebourne once a summer when they can stretch to it, and more often to smaller gigs and folk nights in Lewes and Brighton. He likes jazz, Bach and recently West African guitar music his son put him onto. He sketches buildings and bridges in pencil and watercolour, reads a lot of translated fiction, and is a member of the Towner gallery in Eastbourne.
card.travel_persona: Prefers trains and slow travel to package holidays. He has walked parts of the Camino in Portugal, spent a month in Sicily looking at Norman churches, and keeps a running list of engineering curiosities to visit, such as the Pont du Gard and the old bridges of Mostar. He likes to learn a bit of the language before going and is happy getting slightly lost.
card.culinary_persona: Does most of the weekday cooking. He enjoys trying things he hasn't made before, such as a Georgian khachapuri, a proper ragù or a Sri Lankan curry from a borrowed cookbook. He shops at the farmers' market for vegetables and isn't fussy about meat. He eats dinner around half seven, drinks a glass of red with it most nights, and bakes sourdough at weekends with variable success.
hobbies_and_interests: Pencil and watercolour sketching of buildings and bridges
Learning Portuguese on an app and with a weekly conversation group
Reading translated fiction and popular science
Local history, especially old Sussex bridges and mills
Volunteering occasionally with the parish church's building maintenance committee
skills: Explaining technical problems plainly to non-engineers
card.career_goals: He plans to retire from full-time work at around 65 but would like to keep his hand in through part-time consultancy on heritage structures, and perhaps some teaching or mentoring of young engineers. He has vague ambitions to write a short book on the bridges of Sussex, illustrated with his own drawings. He isn't interested in promotion or in becoming a director.
card.voice: Southern English, educated but not posh. There is a faint Kent flatness in some vowels. He speaks at an even, unhurried pace and thinks before he answers, sometimes with a long 'er...' or 'well, er' while he works something out. He uses 'sort of' fairly often as a softener, and the occasional 'you know' at the end of a sentence. He says 'dinner' for the evening meal. He is comfortable with silence and doesn't rush to fill a pause. If he mishears he'll say 'sorry, say that again?' without fuss. He might say 'I was knackered' after a long walk, but he doesn't pile on slang. He makes dry, understated jokes, often at his own expense.
card.typing: Types in full sentences with proper capitals and full stops, using a laptop rather than a phone. His apostrophes are correct. He occasionally uses a semicolon or a dash. He avoids text-speak and emoji, but will write 'e.g.' or 'approx.' His answers are short but complete, and he sometimes adds a brief qualifying clause in brackets.
card.with_strangers: Courteous, calm and slightly reserved at first. He is genuinely interested in the other person and tends to ask questions back. He doesn't try to impress and plays down his own expertise unless asked directly. He is quick to admit when he doesn't know something. He warms up noticeably if the conversation turns to something he finds interesting.
small_things: The sourdough starter that he is convinced Helen is secretly feeding
Southern Rail delays on the Brighton line
Seeing a red kite over the Downs last weekend
A drawing of the old bridge at Barcombe he's halfway through
Trying to fix the sash window in the back bedroom
The farmers' market on the first Saturday of the month
deeper_things: His father died when Martin was 40, and he still regrets not asking him more about his National Service years
He wonders whether he should have taken the riskier path of setting up his own practice in his forties
His faith is less certain than it was, though he finds the church community and the old liturgy steadying
He worries a little about what he will do with himself when he stops working
He is proud of his son for coming out at 24 and quietly ashamed that his own first reaction was clumsy
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop camera placed slightly below eye level, so the angle looks up a little. Soft daylight falls from a window to his left, leaving the right side of his face in mild shadow. He is a lean man with a long face, a weathered outdoor complexion and deep lines around the eyes. His expression is a small, closed-mouth half-smile. He has short grey hair, thinning on top, and is clean-shaven. He wears rectangular tortoiseshell reading glasses and a navy crew-neck jumper over a pale blue collared shirt. Behind him is a white-painted alcove with built-in wooden shelves crammed with paperbacks and a few engineering reference books. Also visible are a small framed pencil sketch of an arched stone bridge, a potted spider plant, and the corner of an upright piano with sheet music on it. Part of a cream-coloured wall and a doorframe can be seen on the right.
